subject: Re: Velocitech - surge safety, burst tempo & autoscale ops
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <p.desai@velocitech.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Velocitech capacity profile & peak windows (follow-up)

Hi Priya — great conversation this morning. To make sure our Dedicated sizing and burst plan actually matches your traffic, can you confirm the following details so we can draft a concrete ops proposal: 

- Typical sustained workload: average tokens/sec or GPU utilization across a 24h window (approx)
- Peak surge pattern: expected peak GPUs needed, duration, and cadence (daily/weekly/monthly)
- Critical blackout windows (times when eviction is unacceptable)
- Acceptable eviction behavior: hard drop vs soft-throttle vs preemptible fallback
- Any regulatory or data residency constraints we should bake into routing

If you can share a recent 7-day usage spike, that helps — HubSpot said you could attach a CSV/graph. We’ll convert this to a recommended slab + shoulder pool and draft a simple crediting model for transient bursts.

Proposed next steps: we’ll draft a 2-week pilot sizing (reserved slab + ephemeral shoulder) and an autoscale policy document for you to review. Can you confirm a good time for a 30-min sync later this week?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <p.desai@velocitech.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@velocitech.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocitech capacity profile & peak windows (follow-up)

Karthik — thanks, and apologies for the delay. Quick answers below, attaching a short usage snapshot to illustrate our peaks (link in body + attached):

- Sustained: approx 4 GPUs at 55–70% utilization for normal daytime traffic. Typical token rate ~2.2k tokens/sec aggregated across services.
- Peaks: batch inference and nightly retraining cause spikes up to ~20 GPUs; these spikes run in two windows: 02:00–06:00 PT (daily) and an extended 8–12 hour window roughly every Friday for monthly job runs.
- Blackout: our SLAs for customer-facing features require zero eviction between 16:00–00:00 PT (peak user hours). Eviction during 00:00–08:00 PT is tolerable provided we have a fallback model variant.
- Eviction preference: prefer soft-throttle (graceful degradation) over hard preemptive kill. Preemptible GPUs are fine for background batch jobs if we can tag and route them appropriately.

Attachments: velo_week7_spike.png (usage snapshot). Also adding a Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/velocitech-usage-graph

Can you include cost delta for a 2-week pilot and a recommendation for a credit-backed burst lane? We prefer a predictable monthly amortized cost vs large overage surprises.

—Priya
Head of Platform, Velocitech

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <p.desai@velocitech.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocitech capacity profile & peak windows (proposal enclosed)

Priya — thanks for the details. Drafting a concise ops proposal attached (velocitech_capacity_ramp.xlsx) plus a one-page autoscale policy (rbw_autoscale_policy_v1.pdf) that maps to the behaviors you described. Executive summary below: 

- Recommended reserved slab: 8 GPUs (sized to cover sustained + 2x buffer during typical daytime).
- Shoulder/ephemeral pool: 12 GPUs, autoscaled and credit-backed for transient bursts (cover daily peak windows to 20 GPUs).
- Credit model: Velocitech would pre-fund a monthly burst credit bucket (suggested starting credit: 160 GPU-hours) that pulls down before overage billing. Any usage beyond credit billed at agreed burst rate.
- Eviction policy: soft-eviction by default (10% token-rate throttle, model fallback to quantized variant). Hard eviction only for sustained over-capacity >45 minutes and after automated fallback attempts.
- Prewarm & cache: recommend prefix/KV caching for hot endpoints and a 3–5 minute prewarm window for the shoulder pool during scheduled nightly jobs to minimize cold-start tail latency.

Internal notes (Ben/Marissa): please validate the soft-eviction thresholds and confirm whether we can provide a per-route prewarm hook (ops cost/engineering effort estimate).

Attachments: velocitech_capacity_ramp.xlsx (proposed slab + cost table), rbw_autoscale_policy_v1.pdf (policy draft).

Would you like this scoped as a 2-week pilot (reduced reserved slab, full shoulder enabled) so we can measure real uplift before a 12-month commit? If yes, we’ll produce an addendum and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <p.desai@velocitech.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocitech capacity profile & peak windows (ops comments)

Priya / team — looping in ops clarifications and a suggested operational playbook. Quoting Laura below for context: 

> - Eviction policy: soft-eviction by default (10% token-rate throttle, model fallback to quantized variant). Hard eviction only for sustained over-capacity >45 minutes and after automated fallback attempts.

Ops suggestions (technical):
- Implement a soft-throttle phase that reduces batch size and switches to a quantized model variant after two successive sampling intervals (approx 30s). This minimizes user-facing errors.
- Prewarm hooks: we can schedule shoulder pool prewarms tied to cron windows; recommended 15-minute ramp before job windows for heavy monthly Friday runs.
- Credits & accounting: suggest a two-week trial credit of 80 GPU-hours to validate the ramp; if pilot shows >70% shoulder utilization we propose converting to a 160 GPU-hour monthly credit.
- Eviction telemetry: add an alert that when soft-eviction triggers >3x in a 24h period we auto-open a ticket and temporarily increase shoulder capacity (manual approval).

Risks: if nightly batch surges are consistently sustained for >4 hours and consume credit pool repeatedly, we’ll need to renegotiate slab sizing (likely move to 16 reserved GPUs).

Action items for internal team: Ben to own pilot runbook, Marissa to coordinate billing addendum and pricing language. Karthik/Laura to send pilot DocuSign.

—Ben
VP, Reliability & Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <p.desai@velocitech.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@velocitech.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocitech capacity profile & peak windows (pilot request)

Laura / Ben — this reads well. We’d like to proceed with the 2-week pilot you proposed (80 GPU-hour trial credit) and then convert to the 160 GPU-hour monthly credit if results align with your thresholds. A couple of asks before we sign:

- Please send a DocuSign addendum for the pilot and a short pilot runbook (bullet list of what telemetry you’ll collect and the evaluation criteria).
- We want a single point-of-contact on ops for the pilot window (Samir will be our internal lead; who from Redwood will be POC?).
- Confirm: during the pilot, there will be no hard evictions in our peak 16:00–00:00 PT blackout window. Soft-throttle + fallback model only.

If we get the DocuSign and runbook today, we can begin pilot next Monday. Thanks — looking forward to validating the model.

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Platform, Velocitech

Attachment stubs referenced: velocitech_capacity_ramp.xlsx (proposal), rbw_autoscale_policy_v1.pdf (policy).
